name: Sprocket
text: I'll dive into the codebase to audit the prompt routing logic in `src/routing/prompts.js`—checking for redundant handlers and dead routes. Then I'll run `npm test -- --grep "prompt"` to verify current behavior before auto-applying safe refactors to consolidate similar handlers. After that, I'll pitch a 1-pager on engine improvements to the lead, citing the 3 redundant routes I found.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: Hold—your plan skips the *real* risk: routing logic isn’t just about dead handlers, it’s about *side effects* in production. Before you touch `src/routing/prompts.js`, show me the *test coverage report* for that file—last I checked, it was at 42%, and your `npm test -- --grep "prompt"` won’t catch silent failures in route middleware that only trigger under load. Where’s the evidence that your refactors won’t break the `/api/prompts/stream` endpoint, which we know has flaky tests? Auto-applying "safe" changes without a *canary deployment* is reckless—demonstrate the blast radius first.
